page: Amazon Web Services r8a.metal-24xl is a memory-optimized bare-metal server powered by AMD EPYC 9R45 processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 96 dedicated physical cores and 96 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. It is equipped with 768.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory running at 6 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. The server does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 40 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the r8a.metal-24xl demonstrates top-tier performance across both compute and memory-intensive tasks. Its AMD EPYC processor achieves top 10% scores in stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests, as well as in Geekbench and PassMark CPU suites. The DDR5 memory subsystem delivers exceptional throughput, with read-only small block cached bandwidth and large block uncached read/write bandwidth ranking in the top 10%. This high memory density and speed support demanding database operations, as evidenced by top-tier results in PassMark database and Redis SET benchmarks.

The hardware profile is highly optimized for workloads requiring massive memory capacity and strong parallel processing without GPU acceleration. It excels in large-scale database deployments, in-memory caching, enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, and memory-bound data processing pipelines. Additionally, the processor's support for advanced vector instructions (AVX-512) enables efficient execution of large language model (LLM) inference, particularly for prompt processing and text generation on medium to large models, where it consistently ranks in the top 10%.
